about: people who want to get good at using AI at work

scenes.caption: you don't need the whole plan, you need the first step. what are you still waiting to start?
nobody writes the perfect prompt first time, the good ones just write more of them. how many drafts do you allow yourself?
the best answer is almost never the first one. do you ask a follow-up question?
the answer is only as good as the ask. how clear was your last prompt?
someday never shows up on a calendar. what would your day one look like?
one is still fixing the first block, the other is standing on the wall. which one is you this week?
the first answer is a draft, the follow-up is where it gets good. how often do you push back?
ai can't read your mind, tell it who it is for and why. do you give it the background?
watching someone use ai is not the same as using it. how much of your learning is watching?
you learn what works by building it, not by thinking about it. what have you been overthinking?
a bad answer usually means a bad question. do you quit or do you ask it another way?
a four becomes a ten one fix at a time. do you stop at the first try?
the goal is the same, only one of them is moving. what is your next small step?
ai does better with five small asks than one giant one. do you break your tasks down?
ask for ten options and the third one is usually the keeper. how many do you ask for?
ai is confident even when it is wrong. do you check before you paste?
the people ai replaces are the ones who never learned to use it. which side are you on?
ten tools you opened once will not beat one tool you know well. which one do you actually know?
you can wait two days for a reply or get unstuck in two minutes. what are you waiting on right now?
one example of what you want is worth a paragraph of explaining. do you show it what good looks like?
a rough try today teaches more than a perfect plan next month. what could you try today?
done and decent beats perfect and missing. what are you tweaking right now?
when it says it can't, ask why, there is usually a way around. do you stop at no?
trusting ai blindly is how mistakes reach your boss. how do you test what it tells you?
five minutes a day beats the course you never finish. could you spare five minutes?
every restart throws away what you learned. what would happen if you just kept going?
asking the same thing louder does not work on people or on ai. what is another way to ask it?
tell it what was wrong and it fixes it, say nothing and you get the same again. do you tell it?
everyone who is good at this started behind someone. what makes you think it is too late?
good is not an instruction, shorter, friendlier, for a client is. what does good mean to you?
